architecture.summary: SO-11a exports the system log of the hosted control plane to an OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint of the operator, a new external integration; for production the owner chose the Axiom dataset system-log. The control plane reads three new settings at its start: SYSTEM_LOG_OTLP_ENDPOINT (https only), SYSTEM_LOG_OTLP_TOKEN (a secret that the tenant role now refuses), and SYSTEM_LOG_AXIOM_DATASET. All three empty keep the system log on standard error only; one of the endpoint and the token without the other, or an invalid value, stops the start with a message that names the setting and the rule. app owns the export: the entry builds SystemLogOutput, a SystemLogSink that writes each record to ConsoleSystemLogSink and, after the start of the export, to OtelSystemLogSink with the OpenTelemetry SDK (BatchLogRecordProcessor with a queue of 2,048 that drops the newest, a batch every 2 s, OTLPLogExporter with retries within 4 s, the resource service.name thermus-control-plane and service.instance.id from RENDER_INSTANCE_ID). A failed batch is dropped, and one standard error line at most once a minute names its cause through a logger with only the console sink, so a failure cannot feed the export. The stop waits at most 5 s for the last records, after the HTTP server closed and after a FATAL line. The audit sender stays separate, and the system-logs exports do not change. The SDK packages move from devDependencies to dependencies at 0.223.0, and @opentelemetry/resources 2.12.0, already a dependency of the SDK, becomes a direct dependency; the rules list the three packages for app. Since SO-09, the exported lines include the Tenant fleet summary and Organization sweep lines that the monitors of runbook 7.3 read, so the summary queries of the runbook read the field body of the dataset system-log. No component, edge, public module, or declaration changes.
